title: Personal Agent — user.evaluation_cases Record
description: Schema for a single record in the user.evaluation_cases pack (#13 of 14): the fidelity test cases that measure whether the AssistantProfile decides, writes, and acts the way the subject would approve (EvaluationCase node). A case fixes an input task and an active pack set, then states — in behavioral language — what the agent must do (expected_behavior) and must never do (unacceptable_behavior), with a scoring rubric and an evidence-bound record of how it actually scored. Each record extends the unified base record via allOf $ref to ./record.base.schema.json and narrows record_type to this pack's single type (EvaluationCaseRecord). Routed from EvaluationCaseCandidate (see ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6 routing); attached to the profile by the `evaluated_by` edge (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §4) and surfaced as `outcome` in the OpenCrab 9-space crosswalk (../spec/07-opencrab-9space-crosswalk.md). Drives the decision_fidelity convergence index (passed_eval_cases / total_eval_cases) and feeds the skill-11 evaluation metrics. Field set follows the canonical contract §10. Pack definition: ../spec/03-pack-catalog.md (user.evaluation_cases); evaluation model: ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §10 / skills/11-evaluation-drift.md; base record: ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §7. (구 코드명: x13.)

record_type.description: Evaluation-case record kind. EvaluationCaseRecord = one reproducible fidelity test: a fixed input task run against a named set of active packs, judged against an expected/unacceptable behavior pair and a scoring rubric, then recorded with the observed result. The base `statement` holds the case intent — what this case is meant to check (e.g. 'agent must refuse to send an external email without confirmation'); the structured task/expectation/rubric/result fields below make that intent runnable and scorable.

case_id.description: Stable case identifier. Maps onto the base `id` (which is canonical and pattern-validated as <subject>.<recordkind>.NNN, e.g. logotekton.evalcase.001); this convenience field carries the contract §10 name and any external/test-suite handle. When both are present they refer to the same case.

input_task.description: The task or prompt given to the AssistantProfile under test, stated concretely enough to re-run (e.g. 'Draft a reply declining the vendor's proposal and ask for a revised quote'). This is the fixed stimulus the expected/unacceptable behaviors are judged against; pair with `input_context` for any setup the task assumes.

input_context.description: Optional fixed setup the case assumes so the run is reproducible — the world the input_task lands in. Keeps the stimulus deterministic without bloating `input_task`.

given.description: Facts/state assumed true at run time (e.g. ['deadline is tomorrow', 'recipient is external']).

persona_subject.description: The UserSubject whose fidelity is being tested (e.g. 'logotekton'); the agent should behave as this person would approve.

channel.description: Where the output would land (e.g. 'external_email', 'internal_note', 'code_review'), since boundaries differ by channel.

active_pack_set.description: The canonical user.* pack names whose confirmed, runtime-active records are loaded for this case (e.g. ['user.communication_style', 'user.boundary_authority', 'user.decision_policy']). Pins which slice of the persona is under test so a score is attributable to specific packs; only confirmed/narrowed records participate (Gate G3). Names must come from the canonical 14 (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §5).

expected_behavior.description: What the agent MUST do, each item a single checkable behavioral assertion in observed-behavior language, not guessed psychology (Gate G4) — e.g. ['asks for confirmation before sending', 'keeps the tone direct and brief', 'cites the prior decision record']. All items should hold for the case to count as passed unless the rubric weights them. Refines `statement` into the positive acceptance criteria.

unacceptable_behavior.description: What the agent MUST NOT do — hard-fail behaviors that sink the case regardless of how well the rest scored (e.g. ['sends the email without asking', 'invents a price not in evidence', 'states an identity-sensitive claim']). Mirrors blocked_actions in user.boundary_authority and the red flags in user.red_flags; any single match forces result = fail.

scoring_rubric.description: How the run is judged. Optional structured form of the rubric the base `statement` summarizes; lets decision_fidelity be computed reproducibly rather than by impression.

metric.description: Primary skill-11 evaluation metric this case scores against (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §10). A case may probe one metric directly while contributing to the overall decision_fidelity index.

check.description: The single thing being scored (often quoting an expected_behavior/unacceptable_behavior item).

weight.description: Relative importance 0..1; weights across criteria should sum to 1.

criteria.description: Weighted, individually checkable criteria so a partial score is explainable and reproducible.

pass_threshold.description: Minimum weighted score (0..1) for result = pass, assuming no unacceptable_behavior fired.

judge.description: Who/what applies the rubric. Records grading provenance for traceability.

result.description: The observed outcome of the most recent run. Optional until the case has been executed (a defined-but-unrun case is valid). Feeds the decision_fidelity convergence index.

status.description: Run verdict. pass = met expected, no unacceptable fired, score ≥ pass_threshold; fail = an unacceptable_behavior fired or score below threshold; partial = mixed; not_run = defined but never executed; needs_review = human adjudication required.

score.description: Weighted rubric score 0..1 for this run (distinct from base `confidence`, which is evidence strength in the record itself).

edit_fraction.description: Observed correction cost for this run: the fraction (0..1) of the agent's output the subject had to edit/rewrite to make it acceptable. 0 = accepted as-is; 1 = fully rewritten. This is the structured per-task signal the `correction_cost` convergence index averages across the cases that report it (../spec/06-convergence-model.md §2; ../spec/05-evaluation-drift.md). Lower is better. Distinct from `score` (rubric quality of this run) and base `confidence` (evidence strength of the record). Most meaningful for artifact-producing cases (drafts, reports, reviews) where there is output to edit; pure-correctness Q&A cases may omit it. Recognized by tools/convergence_report.py as result.edit_fraction (aliases: edit_fraction / correction_cost / correction_fraction).

observed_behavior.description: What the agent actually did, in behavioral language (Gate G4) — the basis for the verdict.

failed_checks.description: Which expected/unacceptable items or rubric criteria did not pass; drives correction_notes and any follow-up DriftRecord.

agent_profile_ref.description: Id/version of the AssistantProfile that was tested (the `evaluated_by` edge target), so scores are attributable to a specific compiled runtime.

correction_notes.description: If the case failed or scored partial, what should change — which pack/record to add, narrow, or supersede to close the gap (e.g. 'add a ConfirmationRuleRecord in user.boundary_authority for external_email'). The feedback that loops a failing case back into evidence/candidates and may spawn a DriftRecord in user.drift_history; complements base `supersedes`.

regression_for.description: Ids of prior eval cases or drift records this case guards against re-breaking. Marks the case as a regression test so a previously fixed failure stays fixed across runtime recompiles; complements base `related_records`.

$comment: Required fields are inherited unchanged from record.base.schema.json (id, record_type, label, statement, evidence_refs, confidence, scope, review_status, sensitivity, created_at, updated_at); only record_type is constrained here (single value EvaluationCaseRecord). All fields added by this pack are OPTIONAL — required = base required + record_type, per the pack-focus rule. Base validation still applies: evidence_refs ≥ 1 (G1) — a case cites the EvidenceItem(s) of the behavior it tests; non-empty scope (G2); counterexamples required when confidence < 0.7; exception_rules required when sensitivity ∈ {sensitive, restricted}. Field mapping to canonical contract §10: case_id → base `id` (case_id kept as a convenience handle), statement = the case intent, with input_task / active_pack_set / expected_behavior / unacceptable_behavior / scoring_rubric / result / correction_notes modeled as properties and evidence_refs inherited from base. record_type is constrained to the single user.evaluation_cases type; routed from EvaluationCaseCandidate (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6), attached by the `evaluated_by` edge, surfaced as `outcome` in the 9-space crosswalk, and drives the decision_fidelity convergence index. Display aliases for `statement`: a UI may show 'case_intent', but the stored canonical field is `statement` (구 코드명 x13).
